nodes.summary: Given a type $K$ of keys, a type $V$ of values, a number $m$ of slots, and two hash functions $h_1, h_2 : K \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, a cuckoo hash table consists of two tables, each a vector of $m$ slots; every slot is either empty or holds a key–value pair $(k, v)$ with $k \in K$ and $v \in V$. The structure itself does not require a pair $(k, v)$ to sit at slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table or at slot $h_2(k)$ of…
nodes.title: Cuckoo hash table

nodes.summary: The empty cuckoo hash table has every slot of both tables vacant.
nodes.title: Empty cuckoo hash table

nodes.summary: The eviction loop takes a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, a key–value pair $(k, v)$, a choice of the first or second table, and a natural number as fuel, and either returns a table or fails. With fuel $0$ it fails. With fuel $n + 1$ and the first table chosen, it writes $(k, v)$ into slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table; if that slot was empty it returns the resulting table, and otherwise it…
nodes.title: Cuckoo eviction loop

nodes.summary: Inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, with fuel $n$, either returns a table or fails. If slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table holds a binding for $k$, that slot is overwritten with $(k, v)$, and slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table is cleared if it also holds a binding for $k$, so no stale competing value remains. Otherwise, if slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table…
nodes.title: Cuckoo hash insertion

nodes.summary: No key is stored with two different values in the empty cuckoo hash table, vacuously.
nodes.title: The empty cuckoo hash table is key-deterministic

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. If inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ with some fuel succeeds with result $T'$, then $T'$ is key-deterministic. In particular, replacement leaves no stale copy of $k$ with a different value in the other slot.
nodes.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves key determinism

nodes.summary: A cuckoo hash table is key-deterministic when each key is stored with at most one value: for every key $k$ and values $v_1, v_2$, if the bindings $k \mapsto v_1$ and $k \mapsto v_2$ are both stored in the table, then $v_1 = v_2$. Duplicate copies of the same pair are allowed.
nodes.title: Key determinism of a cuckoo hash table

nodes.summary: Looking up any key in the empty cuckoo hash table finds no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty cuckoo hash table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. For every key $k$ and value $v$, looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in $T$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup finds exactly the stored bindings

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. For every key $k$ and value $v$, if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in $T$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup finds every stored binding

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup finds a key in its first-table slot

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$ and slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table of $T$ holds no pair whose key is $k$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup finds a key in its second-table slot

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant and stores each key with at most one value. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then for every key $k' \ne k$, looking up $k'$ in $T'$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$: either both return nothing or both return the same…
nodes.title: Cuckoo insertion leaves lookups of other keys unchanged

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant and stores each key with at most one value. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then looking up $k$ in $T'$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup returns an inserted value

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant, and let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of either table of $T$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns some value.
nodes.title: Cuckoo lookup finds every stored key

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$, then the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of the first or the second table of $T$.
nodes.title: Soundness of cuckoo lookup

nodes.summary: For a cuckoo hash table $T$ with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ and a key $k$, the lookup of $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table holds a pair $(k, v)$; otherwise it returns $v$ if slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table holds a pair $(k, v)$; otherwise it returns nothing. No other slot is examined.
nodes.title: Cuckoo hash table lookup

nodes.summary: A slot of a cuckoo hash table is either empty or holds a pair $(k, v)$ of a key and a value. For a slot $s$ and a key $k'$, this test is true when $s$ holds a pair whose key is $k'$, and false when $s$ is empty or holds a pair with a different key.
nodes.title: Slot holds a key

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant. Suppose inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$. Then for every key $k' \ne k$ and every value $v'$, the binding $k' \mapsto v'$ is stored in $T'$ if and only if it is stored in $T$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves the bindings of other keys

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of either table of $T'$.
nodes.title: Cuckoo insertion stores the inserted binding

nodes.summary: A key $k$ is stored with value $v$ in a cuckoo hash table when the pair $(k, v)$ occupies some slot of the first table or some slot of the second table.
nodes.title: Binding stored in a cuckoo hash table

nodes.summary: For any hash functions $h_1, h_2$ into $m$ slots, the empty cuckoo hash table, with every slot of both tables vacant, satisfies the placement invariant.
nodes.title: The empty cuckoo hash table satisfies the placement invariant

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant. If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ (which replaces an existing binding for $k$ in place) with some fuel bound succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then $T'$ satisfies the placement invariant.
nodes.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves the placement invariant

nodes.summary: A cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1, h_2$ satisfies the placement invariant when every pair $(k, v)$ in slot $i$ of the first table has $i = h_1(k)$, and every pair $(k, v)$ in slot $i$ of the second table has $i = h_2(k)$.
nodes.title: Placement invariant of a cuckoo hash table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
